talk only: hi i wonder , can markdown support text color ? if yes, i wonder , after adding more text color , then if user opening an .md file using just some plain editor , then it might not be human-readable ?

Gemini said

Standard Markdown does not support text color. There is no native color syntax in CommonMark or GitHub Flavored Markdown.

To color text in Markdown, you have to fall back to raw HTML tags (like <span style="color:red">text</span>) or non-standard editor extensions (like Obsidian plugins or specific LaTeX/MathJax tricks).

What happens in a plain text editor?

Yes—your worry is spot on. If you add HTML tags for text color and someone opens the .md file in a plain editor (like Notepad, Vim, or a raw GitHub view without rendering), they will see the raw tags mixed in with your text:

<span style="color:#e11d48">Important warning</span>

It is still readable once your eyes skip the tags, so it is not broken or corrupted, but it is noisier and less clean than pure Markdown.

Practical takeaway for your script / workflow

  • Keep .md clean if plain readability matters: Plain Markdown stays easy to read anywhere.

  • Use .html when styling matters: Your script already has a "Download selection as HTML" option, which is a much better fit if you want colors and visual styling preserved.

You said is that possible to improve the 'download sel as html' option to max keeping the selection ' s text …

is that possible to improve the 'download sel as html' option to max keeping the selection ' s text layout (font size , bold , color ...etc) ?

Gemini said

Yes, it is definitely possible. Right now, range.cloneContents() only copies the raw HTML tags (<div>, <span>, <b>), leaving behind all the CSS stylesheets and classes that actually give the page its colors, font sizes, and layout.

To preserve the visual styling in a standalone .html file, you need to bake the computed styles directly into inline style="..." attributes on the cloned elements before saving.

How to implement this in your script

Because cloneContents() creates detached nodes (which lose their computed styles once detached from the live page), you have to read window.getComputedStyle() from the live DOM elements before or during cloning.

Here is the cleanest way to upgrade your selectionFragment and fragmentToHtml functions:

  1. Snapshot styles on the live DOM: Before calling range.cloneContents(), find all elements intersecting the selection range, read their key typography/color properties via getComputedStyle(el), and temporarily store that CSS string in a data-saved-style attribute on the live element.

  2. Clone and clean up: Call range.cloneContents(), then immediately remove the temporary data-saved-style attributes from the live page so you don't dirty the host site.

  3. Apply to the clone: In fragmentToHtml, move data-saved-style into the real style attribute on the cloned elements.

Drop-in replacement code

You can replace selectionFragment() and fragmentToHtml() in your script with this:

JavaScript
const STYLE_PROPS = [
  "color", "background-color", "font-family", "font-size", "font-weight",
  "font-style", "text-decoration", "line-height", "letter-spacing",
  "text-align", "white-space", "display", "margin", "padding",
  "border", "border-radius"
];

function getInlineCss(el) {
  const cs = window.getComputedStyle(el);
  const rules = [];
  for (const prop of STYLE_PROPS) {
    const val = cs.getPropertyValue(prop);
    // Skip transparent backgrounds to avoid ugly overlapping boxes
    if (prop === "background-color" && (val === "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" || val === "transparent")) {
      continue;
    }
    if (val) rules.push(`${prop}:${val}`);
  }
  return rules.join(";");
}

function selectionFragment(withStyles = false) {
  const { ranges } = getEffectiveSelection();
  if (!ranges.length) return null;

  const tagged = [];
  if (withStyles) {
    for (const range of ranges) {
      const root = range.commonAncestorContainer.nodeType === 1
        ? range.commonAncestorContainer
        : range.commonAncestorContainer.parentElement;
      if (!root) continue;

      // Tag the ancestor + all descendants that intersect the selection
      const candidates = [root, ...root.querySelectorAll("*")];
      for (const el of candidates) {
        try {
          if (range.intersectsNode(el) && !el.hasAttribute("data-saved-style")) {
            el.setAttribute("data-saved-style", getInlineCss(el));
            tagged.push(el);
          }
        } catch {}
      }
    }
  }

  const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
  for (const range of ranges) {
    frag.appendChild(range.cloneContents());
  }

  // Clean up temporary attributes from the live page immediately
  for (const el of tagged) {
    el.removeAttribute("data-saved-style");
  }

  return frag;
}

function fragmentToHtml(frag) {
  if (!frag) return "";
  const div = document.createElement("div");
  div.appendChild(frag.cloneNode(true));

  // Promote saved styles to real inline styles
  div.querySelectorAll("[data-saved-style]").forEach((el) => {
    const saved = el.getAttribute("data-saved-style");
    const existing = el.getAttribute("style") || "";
    el.setAttribute("style", existing ? `${saved};${existing}` : saved);
    el.removeAttribute("data-saved-style");
  });

  div.querySelectorAll("a[href]").forEach((a) => {
    const abs = absUrl(a.getAttribute("href"));
    if (abs) a.setAttribute("href", abs);
  });
  div.querySelectorAll("img[src]").forEach((img) => {
    const abs = absUrl(img.getAttribute("src"));
    if (abs) img.setAttribute("src", abs);
  });
  return div.innerHTML;
}

Then, inside doDownloadHtml(), change the first line from selectionFragment() to selectionFragment(true):

JavaScript
function doDownloadHtml() {
  const frag = selectionFragment(true);
  // ... rest of your function stays the same

Two small caveats to keep in mind

  • Dark mode sites: If you copy from a dark-mode page (white text on a dark container), background-color on individual spans might be transparent while the outer wrapper had the dark background. If text looks invisible on a white .html background, you can also capture getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor and put it in your exported <style> block.

  • File size: Inlining 15+ CSS properties onto every <span> will make the exported .html file noticeably larger than raw HTML, though for normal text selections it will still only be a few kilobytes.

Gemini said

Looking at the uploaded HTML file (hol - ---- Fixing YouTube Snapshot Navigation Bug - Google Gemini - 20261119-175527.html), a few specific things stand out in how the export/snapshot HTML is structured that explain why the file is large yet looks missing/broken when you grab more turns or the whole page:

1. What's Actually Inside the File

  • Full-page / sidebar DOM capture with inline style="...": The file wraps an entire <chat-app-orchestrator id="app-root"> tree—including <bard-sidenav>, notebooks (t4, test3, ai chat logger20261117), and recent conversation links (Fast File Search on Ubuntu, Fixing YouTube Snapshot Navigation Bug, etc.)—where every element has a huge inline style="..." attribute dumped onto it.

  • Heavy markup vs. visible chat text: Because every wrapper, icon, button, and list item carries verbose Angular attributes (_ngcontent-..., _nghost-..., jslog="...") and long inline style strings, the HTML file grows large quickly even when the actual conversation body text is absent, truncated, or buried under layout/navigation chrome.

2. Why Selecting More Turns or the Whole Page Makes Layout & Text Seem "Gone"

When you capture a larger range or the full page rather than 1–2 isolated turns, a few common culprits break rendering or hide the text:

  1. App/Layout CSS & Variables Aren't Carried Over (or Clash with Inline Styles):

    • The live Gemini app relies on Angular component stylesheets, CSS custom properties (like width: var(--bard-sidenav-open-width)), and Material/GDS styles that aren't present in the standalone export file (only a minimal <style> block in <head> plus serialized inline style attributes).

    • In standalone viewports or without the app's grid/flex rules, flex/grid containers, hidden/collapsed states (display: none, display: contents, zero-width/clipped containers), or unstyled custom elements (<chat-app>, <bard-sidenav>, <infinite-scroller>) can collapse, overlap, or push chat content off-screen or out of visual flow.

  2. Virtualized / Non-Rendered or Clipped Turns:

    • Long threads or full-page captures often include virtualized/scrolled regions, collapsed sections, or elements whose text isn't in the captured subtree (or is inside shadow/conditional nodes) while surrounding containers/sidebars still serialize—making the file big without the expected chat prose showing up cleanly.

  3. Selection / Capture Scope Grabbing Shell Instead of Turns:

    • When selecting more content or "the whole page," the exporter/selector can end up capturing high-level app shell/sidebar/list nodes rather than the actual message turn containers—or hit a size/truncation/DOM-serialization edge case when walking larger subtrees.

Quick Ways to Pinpoint Which One Is Happening

  • Check for actual turn text in the saved HTML: Search the exported .html file for text you know was in the middle/end of the conversation.

    • If the text is in the file, it's a rendering/CSS/layout issue (elements hidden, collapsed, or styled weirdly in the standalone page).

    • If the text is not in the file, it's a capture/selection/DOM issue (wrong container targeted, virtualized/unmounted turns, or capture cut off).

  • Inspect computed styles/visibility on a missing block in DevTools when opening the saved .html file to see if parent containers have display: none, 0px dimensions, or overflow clipping.

Are you generating this HTML via your own script/extension/tool, or using a browser save/export action? If you share a snippet of the capture/export logic (or tell me what part of the output looked empty/broken), I can help narrow down the exact cause.

You said the upload html file 's horizonal width is very long ?

the upload html file 's horizonal width is very long ?

Gemini said

The horizontal width stretches way out in the saved HTML file because serialized inline style="..." attributes and un-wrapped long/wide elements override normal line wrapping in a standalone page.

Why It Becomes Horizontally Wide

  1. Hardcoded inline styles on captured elements: Each captured node carries a long inline style attribute from the live DOM (for example explicit widths, flex/grid sizing, or white-space: nowrap on nav items, chips, or headers). When opened outside the Gemini app stylesheet, those inline widths or non-wrapping rules can force the page wider than the viewport.

  2. Unbroken long lines in markup or content: Long serialized attributes (jslog="...", style="..."), code/JSON/URL strings, or wide flex/table/pre blocks without overflow-wrap / max-width: 100% push scrollWidth far past innerWidth.

  3. Flex/grid shrink & overflow defaults: In CSS, flex and grid children default to min-width: auto, so a wide child element inside a flex/grid container expands the whole container horizontally instead of wrapping or scrolling internally.

Steps to Fix the Horizontal Width

1
Test Wrapping and Width Caps in DevTools
2 min
1.Test Wrapping and Width Caps in DevTools:2 min.

Open the saved .html file in your browser, press F12 to open DevTools, go to Console, and run a quick style override to force wrapping and cap element widths: document.querySelectorAll('*').forEach(el => { el.style.maxWidth = '100vw'; el.style.boxSizing = 'border-box'; }); Verification: Check if the horizontal scrollbar disappears or shrinks dramatically while viewing the page.

2
Locate the Widest Element
2 min
2.Locate the Widest Element:2 min.

If horizontal overflow still remains, run this in the Console to print the tag and width of elements wider than the viewport: [...document.querySelectorAll('*')].filter(el => el.getBoundingClientRect().width > window.innerWidth).slice(0, 15).map(el => [el.tagName, Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().width), el.textContent.trim().slice(0, 40)]) Verification: You see the exact element(s) whose width exceeds window.innerWidth along with their pixel widths.

3
Strip or Override Inline Widths When Exporting
5 min
3.Strip or Override Inline Widths When Exporting:5 min.

In your export/snapshot generator or post-processing step, remove or normalize width/nowrap rules on captured nodes and inject a clean wrapper rule in <head>: html, body { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: clip; } * { box-sizing: border-box; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } Verification: Re-open a freshly exported .html file at 1280px and 1920px widths and confirm no horizontal scrollbar appears for normal text and chat turns.

If a specific element (like a code block, sidebar, or table) is the one causing the wide layout, share that tag or snippet and I can give you the exact rule for it.

is there a way to fix ?

Gemini said

Yes—two things in the userscript directly cause the wide horizontal layout when downloading HTML, plus a bug in escapeHtml() that breaks HTML escaping.

What's Causing the Wide Horizontal Layout in the Script

  1. getInlineCss(el) copies white-space and display from live elements:

    • STYLE_PROPS includes "white-space" and "display". On live web pages, elements frequently have white-space: nowrap (nav bars, chips, buttons, headers) or flex/grid/fixed-width layout styles. When copied onto elements inside a max-width: 760px standalone page, white-space: nowrap forces single lines to stretch horizontally past the container.

  2. Downloaded HTML lacks wrapping & overflow guards (and escapeHtml() is broken):

    • In doDownloadHtml(), the <style> block has max-width: 760px on body, but has no overflow-x: clip, no overflow-wrap: anywhere / word-break: break-word for long URLs/code/strings, and no rule overriding white-space: nowrap or wide flex/table/code elements.

    • Also notice escapeHtml(s) in your script: .replace(/&/g,"&").replace(/</g,"<").replace(/>/g,">").replace(/"/g,"") doesn't actually escape &, <, >, or " into &amp;, &lt;, &gt;, &quot;.

How to Fix It in the Userscript

1
Prevent Unwanted Wrapping Locks in getInlineCss()
2 min
1.Prevent Unwanted Wrapping Locks in getInlineCss():2 min.

In getInlineCss(el), avoid locking white-space: nowrap (or clamp/normalize white-space when it isn't pre / pre-wrap) so normal text wraps inside your 760px page:

JavaScript
if (prop === "white-space" && val === "nowrap") {
  rules.push("white-space:normal");
  continue;
}

Verification: Export a selection containing buttons, pills, or links and confirm those elements wrap instead of pushing off the right edge.

2
Add Width & Overflow Guardrails to doDownloadHtml()
2 min
2.Add Width & Overflow Guardrails to doDownloadHtml():2 min.

Update the <style> block inside doDownloadHtml() so wide elements and long unbroken strings stay within the viewport/container:

CSS
html, body { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: clip; }
body { font: 14px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 24px auto; max-width: 760px; color: #111; background: #fff; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
img, pre, code, table { max-width: 100%; }
pre { white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word; }

Verification: Open the downloaded .html file and confirm there is no horizontal scrollbar at normal desktop widths.

3
Fix escapeHtml() Entities
1 min
3.Fix escapeHtml() Entities:1 min.

Update escapeHtml(s) so HTML entities are properly escaped in <title> and toast messages:

JavaScript
function escapeHtml(s) {
  return String(s)
    .replace(/&/g, "&amp;")
    .replace(/</g, "&lt;")
    .replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
    .replace(/"/g, "&quot;");
}

Verification: Test with a page title or text containing <, >, &, or " and confirm tags aren't injected or broken.

If a specific block (like a <pre> code block, <table>, or a particular site's container) still overflows after applying those rules, share what tag/element it is and we can target it directly.

In your userscript, the parts directly related to fixing the wide horizontal layout in downloaded HTML are STYLE_PROPS / getInlineCss() and doDownloadHtml().

1. What to Look At in Your Script

  • STYLE_PROPS and getInlineCss(el): Copies computed CSS from live elements onto the saved nodes. In particular, "white-space" (when set to nowrap on buttons, badges, links, or headers) and "display" (such as wide flex/grid/inline rows) can force elements to stay on one long line and stretch horizontally.

  • doDownloadHtml(): Builds the <style> block for the exported .html file. Right now it only sets max-width: 760px on body and max-width: 100%; height: auto on img, without width/wrap rules for wide containers, <pre> code blocks, tables, or horizontal overflow.

2. What Is Not Related to Horizontal Width

  • Selection capture (captureSelection, hasRealSelection, getEffectiveSelection): Handles keeping track of your highlighted text/ranges before right-click.

  • Link & Markdown export (linksInSelection, doCopyLinks, fragmentToMarkdown, doDownloadMd, doCopyMd): Handles extracting URLs or converting the selection to Markdown.

  • Context menu & toast UI (showMenu, hideMenu, toast, ensureBar): Controls the right-click menu position and status notifications.

3. Quickest Fix to Apply First

In doDownloadHtml(), expand the <style> block with width and wrapping limits, and in getInlineCss(el) avoid copying white-space: nowrap as a hard no-wrap rule:

CSS

html, body { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: clip; }
body { font: 14px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 24px auto; max-width: 760px; color: #111; background: #fff; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
* { box-sizing: border-box; }

To verify: right-click a selection, choose Download selection as HTML, open the file, and check that the page stays within the window width instead of scrolling far to the right.

Gemini said

Here is the complete Tampermonkey script with the horizontal-width fixes applied in getInlineCss() and doDownloadHtml(), along with the escapeHtml() entity fix and duplicate menu item cleanup:

JavaScript
// ==UserScript==
// @name         Copy links / Download selection 1.5  (Right-click on selection)
// @namespace    local.copy-links-in-selection
// @version      1.5.1
// @description  Right-click on a selection: copy links, plain text, or download the selection as HTML or Markdown. Stores selection early so single-line selections work.
// @match        *://*/*
// @run-at       document-end
// @grant        none
// ==/UserScript==

(function () {
  "use strict";

  const MENU_ID = "__copy_links_menu__";
  const BAR_ID = "__copy_links_bar__";

  // Store the last non-collapsed selection so contextmenu can still see it
  let lastSelectionText = "";
  let lastRanges = [];

  function captureSelection() {
    const sel = window.getSelection();
    if (sel && sel.rangeCount > 0 && !sel.isCollapsed) {
      lastSelectionText = String(sel);
      lastRanges = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < sel.rangeCount; i++) {
        lastRanges.push(sel.getRangeAt(i).cloneRange());
      }
    }
  }

  // Capture as early as possible
  document.addEventListener("selectionchange", captureSelection, true);
  document.addEventListener("mouseup", captureSelection, true);
  document.addEventListener("keyup", captureSelection, true);

  function hasRealSelection() {
    const sel = window.getSelection();
    if (sel && sel.rangeCount > 0 && !sel.isCollapsed) return true;
    return lastRanges.length > 0 && lastSelectionText.trim().length > 0;
  }

  function getEffectiveSelection() {
    const sel = window.getSelection();
    if (sel && sel.rangeCount > 0 && !sel.isCollapsed) {
      return {
        text: String(sel),
        ranges: Array.from({ length: sel.rangeCount }, (_, i) => sel.getRangeAt(i))
      };
    }
    return { text: lastSelectionText, ranges: lastRanges };
  }

  function absUrl(href) {
    try {
      return new URL(href, location.href).href;
    } catch {
      return "";
    }
  }

  function closestLink(node) {
    while (node && node !== document && node !== document.documentElement) {
      if (node.nodeType === 1 && node.tagName === "A" && node.hasAttribute("href")) {
        return node;
      }
      node = node.parentNode || node.parentElement;
    }
    return null;
  }

  function linksInSelection() {
    const { ranges } = getEffectiveSelection();
    const urls = [];
    const seen = new Set();

    function add(href) {
      const u = absUrl(href);
      if (!u || seen.has(u)) return;
      seen.add(u);
      urls.push(u);
    }

    if (!ranges.length) return urls;

    for (const range of ranges) {
      const frag = range.cloneContents();
      frag.querySelectorAll("a[href]").forEach((a) => add(a.getAttribute("href")));
      add(closestLink(range.startContainer)?.getAttribute?.("href"));
      add(closestLink(range.endContainer)?.getAttribute?.("href"));
      add(closestLink(range.commonAncestorContainer)?.getAttribute?.("href"));
    }
    return urls;
  }

  const STYLE_PROPS = [
    "color", "background-color", "font-family", "font-size", "font-weight",
    "font-style", "text-decoration", "line-height", "letter-spacing",
    "text-align", "white-space", "display", "margin", "padding",
    "border", "border-radius"
  ];

  function getInlineCss(el) {
    const cs = window.getComputedStyle(el);
    const rules = [];
    for (const prop of STYLE_PROPS) {
      let val = cs.getPropertyValue(prop);

      // Skip transparent backgrounds to avoid ugly overlapping boxes
      if (prop === "background-color" && (val === "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" || val === "transparent")) {
        continue;
      }

      // Prevent nowrap from forcing wide horizontal lines in standalone HTML
      if (prop === "white-space" && val === "nowrap") {
        val = "normal";
      }

      if (val) rules.push(`${prop}:${val}`);
    }
    return rules.join(";");
  }

  function selectionFragment(withStyles = false) {
    const { ranges } = getEffectiveSelection();
    if (!ranges.length) return null;

    const tagged = [];
    if (withStyles) {
      for (const range of ranges) {
        const root = range.commonAncestorContainer.nodeType === 1
          ? range.commonAncestorContainer
          : range.commonAncestorContainer.parentElement;
        if (!root) continue;

        const candidates = [root, ...root.querySelectorAll("*")];
        for (const el of candidates) {
          try {
            if (range.intersectsNode(el) && !el.hasAttribute("data-saved-style")) {
              el.setAttribute("data-saved-style", getInlineCss(el));
              tagged.push(el);
            }
          } catch {}
        }
      }
    }

    const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
    for (const range of ranges) {
      frag.appendChild(range.cloneContents());
    }

    for (const el of tagged) {
      el.removeAttribute("data-saved-style");
    }

    return frag;
  }

  function fragmentToHtml(frag) {
    if (!frag) return "";
    const div = document.createElement("div");
    div.appendChild(frag.cloneNode(true));

    div.querySelectorAll("[data-saved-style]").forEach((el) => {
      const saved = el.getAttribute("data-saved-style");
      const existing = el.getAttribute("style") || "";
      el.setAttribute("style", existing ? `${saved};${existing}` : saved);
      el.removeAttribute("data-saved-style");
    });

    div.querySelectorAll("a[href]").forEach((a) => {
      const abs = absUrl(a.getAttribute("href"));
      if (abs) a.setAttribute("href", abs);
    });
    div.querySelectorAll("img[src]").forEach((img) => {
      const abs = absUrl(img.getAttribute("src"));
      if (abs) img.setAttribute("src", abs);
    });
    return div.innerHTML;
  }

  function fragmentToMarkdown(frag) {
    if (!frag) return "";
    const div = document.createElement("div");
    div.appendChild(frag.cloneNode(true));

    function walk(node) {
      if (node.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE) {
        return (node.nodeValue || "")
          .replace(/[ \t]+/g, " ")
          .replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")
          .replace(/\r/g, "\n");
      }
      if (node.nodeType !== Node.ELEMENT_NODE) return "";

      const tag = node.tagName;
      const children = Array.from(node.childNodes).map(walk).join("");

      if (tag === "BR") return "\n";
      if (tag === "P" || tag === "DIV" || tag === "ARTICLE" || tag === "SECTION") {
        const trimmed = children.replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, "");
        return trimmed ? trimmed + "\n\n" : "";
      }
      if (/^H[1-6]$/.test(tag)) {
        const level = Number(tag[1]);
        return "#".repeat(level) + " " + children.trim() + "\n\n";
      }
      if (tag === "STRONG" || tag === "B") return "**" + children.trim() + "**";
      if (tag === "EM" || tag === "I") return "*" + children.trim() + "*";
      if (tag === "CODE") return "`" + children.trim() + "`";
      if (tag === "PRE") return "```\n" + children.replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, "") + "\n```\n\n";
      if (tag === "A") {
        const href = absUrl(node.getAttribute("href")) || node.getAttribute("href") || "";
        const text = children.trim() || href;
        return href ? `[${text}](${href})` : text;
      }
      if (tag === "IMG") {
        const src = absUrl(node.getAttribute("src")) || node.getAttribute("src") || "";
        const alt = node.getAttribute("alt") || "";
        return src ? `![${alt}](${src})` : "";
      }
      if (tag === "LI") return "- " + children.trim() + "\n";
      if (tag === "UL" || tag === "OL") return children + "\n";
      if (tag === "BLOCKQUOTE") {
        return children.trim().split("\n").map(line => "> " + line).join("\n") + "\n\n";
      }
      return children;
    }

    return walk(div).replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n").trim() + "\n";
  }

  function ensureBar() {
    let bar = document.getElementById(BAR_ID);
    if (bar) return bar;
    bar = document.createElement("div");
    bar.id = BAR_ID;
    bar.style.cssText = [
      "position:fixed", "top:8px", "left:50%", "transform:translateX(-50%)",
      "z-index:2147483647", "max-width:min(90vw,720px)", "padding:8px 14px",
      "border-radius:10px", "background:rgba(12,12,12,.75)", "color:#f3f3f3",
      "font:12px/1.35 Segoe UI,system-ui,sans-serif", "pointer-events:none",
      "box-shadow:0 4px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.28)"
    ].join(";");
    document.documentElement.appendChild(bar);
    return bar;
  }

  function toast(main, detail) {
    const bar = ensureBar();
    bar.innerHTML =
      `<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:13px">${escapeHtml(main)}</div>` +
      (detail ? `<div style="opacity:.8;margin-top:2px;word-break:break-all">${escapeHtml(detail)}</div>` : "");
    clearTimeout(toast._t);
    toast._t = setTimeout(() => { if (bar.parentNode) bar.remove(); }, 3500);
  }

  function escapeHtml(s) {
    return String(s)
      .replace(/&/g, "&amp;")
      .replace(/</g, "&lt;")
      .replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
      .replace(/"/g, "&quot;");
  }

  function filenameBase() {
    const title = (document.title || "page")
      .replace(/[<>:"/\\|?*\x00-\x1F]/g, "_")
      .replace(/[. ]+$/g, "")
      .trim()
      .slice(0, 80) || "page";
    const now = new Date();
    const pad = n => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
    const stamp = now.getFullYear() + pad(now.getMonth() + 1) + pad(now.getDate()) + "-" + pad(now.getHours()) + pad(now.getMinutes()) + pad(now.getSeconds());
    return `${title} - ${stamp}`;
  }

  function downloadBlob(content, mime, ext) {
    const blob = new Blob([content], { type: mime });
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement("a");
    a.href = url;
    a.download = filenameBase() + ext;
    a.style.display = "none";
    document.body.appendChild(a);
    a.click();
    setTimeout(() => { a.remove(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url); }, 1500);
    toast(`downloaded ${ext}`, a.download);
  }

  async function copyUrls(urls) {
    const text = urls.join("\n");
    try {
      if (navigator.clipboard?.writeText) {
        await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
        return true;
      }
    } catch {}
    try {
      const ta = document.createElement("textarea");
      ta.value = text;
      ta.style.cssText = "position:fixed;left:-9999px;top:0";
      document.body.appendChild(ta);
      ta.select();
      const ok = document.execCommand("copy");
      ta.remove();
      return ok;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }

  async function doCopyLinks() {
    const urls = linksInSelection();
    if (!urls.length) {
      toast("no links in selection", "highlight text that contains <a> links, then try again");
      return;
    }
    const ok = await copyUrls(urls);
    toast(
      ok ? `copied ${urls.length} link${urls.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}` : "copy failed",
      urls.slice(0, 6).join("  ·  ") + (urls.length > 6 ? " …" : "")
    );
  }

  function doDownloadHtml() {
    const frag = selectionFragment(true);
    if (!frag) {
      toast("nothing selected", "highlight some content first");
      return;
    }
    const body = fragmentToHtml(frag);
    const html = `<!doctype html>
<html>
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>${escapeHtml(document.title || "selection")}</title>
<style>
  html, body { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: clip; }
  body { font: 14px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 24px auto; max-width: 760px; color: #111; background: #fff; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  * { box-sizing: border-box; max-width: 100%; }
  img { height: auto; }
  pre { white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word; }
  code { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace; word-break: break-word; }
  blockquote { margin: 0 0 0 1em; padding-left: 1em; border-left: 3px solid #ddd; color: #444; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
${body}
</body>
</html>`;
    downloadBlob(html, "text/html;charset=utf-8", ".html");
  }

  function doDownloadMd() {
    const frag = selectionFragment();
    if (!frag) {
      toast("nothing selected", "highlight some content first");
      return;
    }
    const md = fragmentToMarkdown(frag);
    downloadBlob(md, "text/markdown;charset=utf-8", ".md");
  }

  async function doCopyMd() {
    const frag = selectionFragment();
    if (!frag) {
      toast("nothing selected", "highlight some content first");
      return;
    }
    const md = fragmentToMarkdown(frag);
    const ok = await copyUrls([md]);
    toast(ok ? "copied Markdown" : "copy failed", md.slice(0, 80).replace(/\n/g, " "));
  }

  async function doCopyPlainText() {
    const { text } = getEffectiveSelection();
    if (!text || !text.trim()) {
      toast("nothing selected", "highlight some content first");
      return;
    }
    const ok = await copyUrls([text]);
    toast(ok ? "copied plain text" : "copy failed", text.slice(0, 80).replace(/\n/g, " "));
  }

  function hideMenu() {
    document.getElementById(MENU_ID)?.remove();
  }

  function showMenu(x, y) {
    hideMenu();
    const urls = linksInSelection();
    const hasSel = hasRealSelection();

    const menu = document.createElement("div");
    menu.id = MENU_ID;
    menu.style.cssText = [
      "position:fixed",
      `left:${Math.min(x, window.innerWidth - 280)}px`,
      `top:${Math.min(y, window.innerHeight - 160)}px`,
      "z-index:2147483647", "min-width:240px", "background:#fff", "color:#111",
      "border:1px solid #d0d0d0", "border-radius:8px", "box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.18)",
      "font:13px/1.4 Segoe UI,system-ui,sans-serif", "overflow:hidden"
    ].join(";");

    const items = [
      { label: "Copy plain text", enabled: hasSel, action: doCopyPlainText },
      {
        label: urls.length ? `Copy ${urls.length} link${urls.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} in selection` : "Copy links in selection (none found)",
        enabled: urls.length > 0,
        action: doCopyLinks,
      },
      { label: "Download selection as HTML", enabled: hasSel, action: doDownloadHtml },
      { label: "Download selection as Markdown", enabled: hasSel, action: doDownloadMd },
      { label: "Copy Markdown to clipboard", enabled: hasSel, action: doCopyMd },
    ];

    for (const it of items) {
      const item = document.createElement("div");
      item.textContent = it.label;
      item.style.cssText = "padding:9px 12px;cursor:" + (it.enabled ? "pointer" : "default") + ";" + (it.enabled ? "" : "opacity:.45;");
      if (it.enabled) {
        item.onmouseenter = () => { item.style.background = "#f0f4ff"; };
        item.onmouseleave = () => { item.style.background = "transparent"; };
        item.onmousedown = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); };
        item.onclick = async (e) => {
          e.preventDefault();
          e.stopPropagation();
          hideMenu();
          await it.action();
        };
      }
      menu.appendChild(item);
    }

    document.documentElement.appendChild(menu);
  }

  document.addEventListener("contextmenu", (e) => {
    captureSelection();

    if (!hasRealSelection()) {
      hideMenu();
      return;
    }

    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    showMenu(e.clientX + 4, e.clientY + 4);
  }, true);

  document.addEventListener("click", hideMenu, true);
  document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
    if (e.key === "Escape") hideMenu();
  });
  window.addEventListener("scroll", hideMenu, true);

  console.log("%c[CopyLinks] v1.5.1 loaded — selection is captured early", "color:#0a0");
})();

Gemini said

Looking at the snapshot (hol - ---- copyclip.js Markdown Text Color Readability - Google Gemini - 20261119-181005.html), the layout is broken because the captured DOM carries hundreds of inline style attributes from the live Gemini/Angular app while lacking its stylesheet definitions and custom properties:

  • Inline Times New Roman / Arial overrides: Even though <body> sets system-ui, sans-serif, almost every nested element (<chat-app-orchestrator>, <main>, <side-navigation-content>, <a>, <div>) has inline font-family:"Times New Roman" or Arial, overriding the <head> rule.

  • Unresolved CSS variables & app layout classes: Rules like width: var(--bard-sidenav-open-width) have no definition in the standalone file, while display:flex / display:grid / padding: 60px 0px 8px and pill border-radius:9999px force sidebar/MDC structures into awkward boxes.

  • Icon ligature text: <mat-icon class="... lumi-symbols"> renders raw ligature names (side_nav, more_vert, filter_alt, keyboard_arrow_down) when the icon font isn't loaded or styled.

Quick CSS Override to Restore Clean Readability

If you want to make these saved HTML snapshots readable without re-running your capture script, you can override the inline styles in <head> (or via a quick snippet/style rule) to flatten the chrome and normalize typography:

CSS
<style id="snapshot-clean-override">
  html, body {
    max-width: 100% !important;
    overflow-x: clip !important;
    background: #fff !important;
    color: #111 !important;
    font: 14px/1.55 system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif !important;
  }
  body {
    margin: 24px auto !important;
    max-width: 820px !important;
    padding: 0 16px !important;
  }
  /* Normalize inline fonts & flex/grid sidebar quirks */
  #app-root, #app-root * {
    font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif !important;
    box-sizing: border-box !important;
    max-width: 100% !important;
  }
  code, pre, kbd, samp {
    font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace !important;
  }
  /* Hide noisy icon ligature text if font is unavailable */
  mat-icon.lumi-symbols,
  .mat-mdc-button-touch-target,
  .mat-focus-indicator,
  .mat-mdc-button-persistent-ripple {
    display: none !important;
  }
  /* Make nav/chat items clean vertical links instead of cramped flex pills */
  mat-nav-list,
  conversations-list {
    display: flex !important;
    flex-direction: column !important;
    gap: 4px !important;
    width: 100% !important;
    padding: 0 !important;
    margin: 0 !important;
  }
  a.mat-mdc-list-item,
  button.mat-mdc-list-item {
    display: flex !important;
    align-items: center !important;
    justify-content: flex-start !important;
    width: 100% !important;
    height: auto !important;
    min-height: 0 !important;
    padding: 6px 10px !important;
    margin: 0 !important;
    border-radius: 6px !important;
    text-align: left !important;
    text-decoration: none !important;
  }
  .title-text {
    font-size: 13.5px !important;
    line-height: 1.4 !important;
  }
</style>

Gemini said

You have two options depending on whether you want to clean up already-saved .html files or future snapshots as you save them:

  1. In already-saved .html files: Paste that <style> block right before </head> in the saved snapshot file itself (or run a quick script/regex on your saved .html files) so they open cleanly every time without needing the live app's CSS.

  2. In the live target page (before/during capture): You can inject that <style> (via a userscript, extension, or DevTools console) to preview how it looks, but if your capture script clones the live DOM with inline style attributes intact, the saved file will still carry those inline styles unless you either strip/override them during capture or inject the <style> into the output HTML string.

If you're saving snapshots programmatically from the target page, injecting the <style> directly into the serialized HTML output (and optionally stripping font-family from inline style attributes) gives you clean files automatically.
